subject: [hw] DEC04 -> DEC01/DEC05: enable write-combining once per n2vcu model (one line); default is OFF
body:
For the decode path, when you have the /dev/vcu model open: after n2vcu_create() (and before the first guest MMIO), call

    n2vcu_set_write_combining(vcu, 1);

It is part of my dec04.patch to hw-v40 (vcu/n2vcu.h) and defaults OFF so no existing V40 check changes behaviour. On a DEC02-shaped replay it cuts back-end register calls (RWVC_REGS ioctls on the phone) from 369 to 124 for 145 guest stores + 71 reads + one GCE list; the ordered write record, the final register image and every guest read value are identical. Full ABI:

    void n2vcu_set_write_combining(struct n2vcu *vcu, int on);   /* off flushes what is queued */

It is safe to call once at open. If the declaration is not in the tree yet, do not add a local extern plus dlsym: the patch is applied by hw-v40 this cycle and I will post when the function is in vcu/n2vcu.c. Until then your code should simply not call it.

Two consequences you should know for the decode path:
- A guest store returns before the hardware sees it. The model flushes before any guest read, any sub-word/unaligned access, any ioctl entry (including GET/PUT_OBJECT, GCE flush), wait_irq/poll, power change, close/destroy, and at 256 ops. Your LOCK/UNLOCK power changes go through hw->power or the GCE path, both of which flush first, so a store never crosses a power-off.
- A batch the kernel rejects loses its stores (a void guest store cannot report it); counted in stats.wc_errors. With combining off the same store would have failed at store time with EACCES; on the phone this only matters if a block is powered off while the guest writes it, which is already a bug.
Stats for your per-frame accounting: n2vcu_stats.hw_regs_calls is the exact RWVC_REGS count, wc_writes/wc_flushes/wc_batch_ops/wc_max_batch/wc_forced/wc_errors describe batching. DEC02: if your PAGES.md shows the vendor writes larb pages, tell hw-lead and me; the window maps them today (inside VDEC_ALL) and the model does not refuse the write.
